DAILY FLOOD BULLETIN 05-AUG-2026

Issued: 05 Aug 2026, 11:15  ·  Published: 05 Aug 2026, 11:22
Download PDF
GOVERNMENT OF PAKISTAN
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE (DEFENCE DIVISION)
PAKISTAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT
FLOOD FORECASTING DIVISION
46-JAIL ROAD LAHORE-54000
BULLETIN No: 052/26 Dated: 5th August-2026 Time: 11:15 hours (PST)

RIVERS AT A GLANCE

FLOOD SEVERITY SCALE

RAINFALL FORECAST — NEXT 24 & 48 HOURS

RIVERS SITUATION AND QUALITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST

I. METEOROLOGICAL FEATURES 

  • Yesterday’s westerly wave over north Afghanistan today lies over northeast Afghanistan. 

  • The upper-air cyclonic circulation associated with yesterday's low-pressure system over northeastern Rajasthan (India) has moved eastwards and presently lies over the central parts of Uttar Pradesh (India).

  • Seasonal low-pressure area lies over northwest Balochistan.

  • Weak moist currents from Arabian sea are penetrating into lower half of the country up to 3,000 feet.

II. METEOROLOGICAL OUTLOOK              

  • Isolated thunderstorm/rain is expected over Islamabad, upper Punjab, Kashmir, and upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during next 24-hours. 

 

III. HYDROLOGICAL SITUATION at 0600 PST

  • River Indus at Kalabagh, Chashma and Guddu is in Low flood level at downstream.

  • All other major rivers are flowing in their normal flows at other gauging stations.

IV. HYDROLOGICAL OUTLOOK

  • No significant change.

V. WEATHER FORECAST FOR 24-HOURS

  • Isolated rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad, Kashmir, 

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Batagram, Buner, Dir, Haripur, Kohistan, Malakand, Mansehra, Mardan, Shangla, Tor Ghar, Swabi and Swat. 

Punjab: Gujrat, Jhelum, Narowal, Rawalpindi and Sialkot. 

Gilgit-Baltistan: Darel, Diamir, Ghizer, Gilgit, Hunza, Nagar and Tangir. 

 

VI. WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR NEXT 48-HOURS

  • Isolated rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad, Kashmir,

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Batagram, Buner, Chitral, Dir, DI Khan, Haripur, Karak, Khyber, Kohat, Kohistan, Lakki Marwat, Mansehra, Nowshera, Orakzai, Peshawar, Shangla, Swabi, Swat and Tor Ghar. 

Punjab: Attock, Chakwal, DG Khan, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Jhelum, Lahore, Layyah, Mandi Bahauddin, Mianwali, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Narowal, Rawalpindi, Sheikhupura and Sialkot. 

Gilgit-Baltistan: Darel, Diamir, Gupis and Tangir.

 

WEEKLY SIGNIFICANT OUTLOOK 

(06th August, 2026 to 12th August, 2026)

I. RAINFALL OUTLOOK

  • Current meteorological conditions and analysis indicate that a fresh wet spell is likely to commence from 8th August. Under the influence of upcoming weather system moderate to heavy rainfalls are expected over Punjab & northeast Sindh. 

II. FLOOD OUTLOOK

  • Flows are likely to increase in eastern rivers, their associated nullahs and hill torrents of DG Khan from 08th August. 

Page break

3. WEATHER/RAINFALL FORECAST FOR NEXT 24-HRS

4. QUANTITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST OF GAUGING STATIONS (IN THOUSANDS OF CUSECS)

Spatial: Isolated=20 to 30% of area | Scattered=31 to 50% of area | Fairly Widespread=51 to 75% of area | Widespread=76 to 100% of area, R= Rising, F=Falling

Intensity (mm/24 hours): Light ≤ 10, Moderate =10.1 – 30, Heavy=30.1 – 70, Very Heavy=70.1 - 150, Extremely Heavy > 150

Note: Concerned Departments may contact FFD, Lahore for rectification up-dation (if any)

5. HOW CLOSE IS EACH RIVER TO ITS LIMIT?

Kalabagh is in low flood at 340.3 — 34.7 below its medium flood level (375.0). Each bar is one station’s own flood levels across its maximum capacity; the solid run is the flow so far, the pale run is the room still left.

All figures in thousands of cusecs. Full bar = maximum (design) capacity. Solid colour is the flow reached so far and the pale wash beside it is the room still left; the dark line between them is the current reading, printed beneath it. Thin white lines are that station’s flood levels with their thresholds beneath, so the same colour can begin at a different point on every bar. Each band is named inside itself — initialled (BL, L, M, H, VH, EH) where the band is too narrow for the words, and left blank where it is too narrow for those. Stations without a design capacity are not shown.

 

 

6. RAINFALL RECORDED — LAST 24-HRS (UPTO 0800 PST)

 

7. RIVERS CATCHMENTS RAINFALL RECORDED (MM) DURING LAST 24-HRS (UPTO 0800 PST)

 (Muhammad Aleem ul Hassan)
Chief Meteorologist
FFD Lahore

III. HYDROLOGICAL SITUATION at 0600 PST

  • River Indus at Kalabagh, Chashma and Guddu is in Low flood level at downstream.

Bulletin DAILY FLOOD BULLETIN 03-AUG-2026
Issued: 03 Aug 2026, 12:45
GOVERNMENT OF PAKISTAN
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE (DEFENCE DIVISION)
PAKISTAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT
FLOOD FORECASTING DIVISION
46-JAIL ROAD LAHORE-54000
BULLETIN No: 050/26 Dated: 3rd August-2026 Time: 12:45 hours (PST)

RIVERS AT GLANCE

FLOOD SEVERITY SCALE  

RAINFALL FORECAST — NEXT 24 & 48 HOURS

RIVERS SITUATION AND QUALITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST

I. METEOROLOGICAL FEATURES 

  • Yesterday’s westerly wave over north Afghanistan persists and its shallow trough is affecting northern parts of the country. 

  • Yesterday’s well marked low over central Rajasthan (India) has weakened into low pressure system and today lies over west Rajasthan (India) with central pressure of 997 hPa.

  • Vertically elongated seasonal low-pressure area lies over northwest Balochistan.

  • Moderate moist currents from Arabian sea and Bay of Bengal (along the foot hills of Himalayan mountains) are penetrating into central and upper parts of the country up to 5,000 feet.

II. METEOROLOGICAL OUTLOOK              

  • Under the influence of low-pressure system, currently lying over west Rajasthan (India) with moderate supporting monsoon currents coupled with shallow trough of westerly wave, a wet spell in which isolated heavy falls are expected over Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northeast Balochistan during next 24 to 36 hours. 

     

III. HYDROLOGICAL SITUATION at 0600 PST

  • River Indus at Kalabagh, Guddu and Sukkur in Low flood level at downstream.

  • River Ravi at Balloki is in Low flood level at upstream.

IV. HYDROLOGICAL OUTLOOK

        WARNING (Up till 06th August): 

  • River Chenab at Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad is expected to fluctuate between Low to Medium flood level during the period.

  • Medium to High level flows are expected in nullahs of Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Bassanter, Deg and Sakki). 

  • Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of DG Khan, the streams of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, river Kabul and its associated tributaries, and northern Balochistan.

  • Urban Flooding is also expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal and Faisalabad. 

V. WEATHER FORECAST FOR 24-HOURS

  • Widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy falls is expected is expected over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad & Kashmir,

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Bajaur, Bannu, Batagram, Buner, Charsadda, Chitral, DI Khan, Dir, Hangu, Haripur, Karak, Khyber, Kohat, Kohistan, Kurram, Lakki Marwat, Malakand, Mansehra, Mardan, Mohmand, Nowshera, Orakzai, Peshawar, Shangla, Waziristan, Swabi, Swat, Tank and Tor Ghar. 

Punjab: Rawalpindi, Attock, Bahawalnagar, Bhakkar, Chakwal, Chiniot, Dera Ghazi Khan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, Jhang, Jhelum, Kasur, Khushab, Lahore, Layyah, Mandi Bahauddin, Mianwali, Nankana Sahib, Narowal, Okara, Pakpattan, Rajanpur, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Toba Tek Singh and Vehari. 

Balochistan: Musakhel, Sherani and Zhob. 

Gilgit-Baltistan: Astore, Darel, Diamir, Ghizer, Gilgit, Gupis-Yasin, Hunza, Nagar and Tangir. 

 

VI. WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR NEXT 48-HOURS

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy falls is expected over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad & Kashmir,

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Buner, DI Khan, Haripur, Lakki Marwat, Mansehra, Mardan, Nowshera, Waziristan, Swabi, Tank and Tor Ghar. 

Punjab: Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Kasur, Khanewal, Lahore, Layyah, Lodhran, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Nankana Sahib, Narowal, Okara, Pakpattan, Rahim Yar Khan, Rajanpur, Rawalpindi, Sahiwal, Sheikhupura, Sialkot and Vehari. 

Balochistan: Barkhan, Musakhel, Sherani and Zhob.

Gilgit-Baltistan: Kharmang and Skardu.

  • Isolated rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy falls is expected over

Bulletin DAILY FLOOD BULLETIN 31-JUL-2026
Issued: 31 Jul 2026, 12:15
GOVERNMENT OF PAKISTAN
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE (DEFENCE DIVISION)
PAKISTAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT

BULLETIN No: 047/26 Dated: 31st July-2026 Time: 12:15 hours (PST)

Rivers at a glance

Flood severity scale 

RAINFALL FORECAST — NEXT 24 & 48 HOURS

RIVERS SITUATION AND QUALITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST

I. METEOROLOGICAL FEATURES 

  • Yesterday's trough of westerly wave is still affecting upper parts of the country.

  • A fresh westerly wave lies over north of Iran.

  • Yesterday’s Deep Depression over west Chattisgarh and adjoining Madhya Pradesh (India) has transformed into Depression and today lies over south Madhya Pradesh and is likely to move westwards over southwest Madhya Pradesh and adjoining Gujarat (India) during next 24-hours.

  • Seasonal low-pressure area lies over Northwest Balochistan.

  • Moderate moist currents from Arabian sea and Bay of Bengal (alongside the foot hills of Himalayan mountains) are penetrating into upper parts of the country up to 5,000 feet.

 

II. METEOROLOGICAL OUTLOOK              

  • In the presence of westerly weather system coupled with monsoon currents from Arabian sea and Bay of Bengal, widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy to very heavy falls is expected uptill 04th August, 

  • Under the influence of an approaching depression (currently lying over south Madhya Pradesh (India)), a strong wet spell in which heavy to very falls are expected over south Punjab, central and eastern parts of Sindh and eastern Balochistan from 1st to 4th August. 

 

III. HYDROLOGICAL SITUATION at 0600 PST

  • River Indus at Guddu is in Medium flood level, whereas at Kalabagh, Chashma and Sukkur is in Low flood level at downstream.

  • River Ravi at Balloki is in Low flood level at upstream.

  • River Indus at Sukkur is in Medium flood level at upstream.

 

IV. HYDROLOGICAL OUTLOOK

  • River Indus at Sukkur will remain in Medium flood level and flows at Guddu will gradually fall from Medium to Low flood level during next 24-hours. 

WARNING:

  • River Chenab at Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad is expected to fluctuate between Low to Medium flood level and may attain High flood level at Marala during the period.

  • Medium to High level flows are expected in nullahs of Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Bassanter, Deg and Sakki). 

  • Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of DG Khan, the streams of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan.

  • Urban Flooding is also expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisalabad. 

  • Urban flooding, water logging and prolonged water ponding is expected in Badin, Hyderabad, Jamshoro, Khairpur, Matiari, Mirpur Khas, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazir Abad, Sujawal, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta and Umer Kot during the period.

 

V. WEATHER FORECAST FOR 24-HOURS

  • Widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy to very heavy fallsis expected over the upper catchments of rivers Sutlej, Ravi and Chenab, Islamabad, Kashmir 

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Haripur, Karak, Kohat, Nowshera and Swabi.

Sindh: Badin, Hyderabad, Jamshoro, Matiari, Mirpur Khas, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazir Abad, Sujawal, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta and Umer Kot. 

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy fall is expected over the upper catchments of rivers Indus and Jhelum,

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Bajaur, Bannu, Batagram, Buner, Charsadda, Chitral, Dir, DI Khan, Hangu, Khyber, Kohistan, Kurram, Lakki Marwat, Malakand, Mansehra, Mardan, Mohmand, North Waziristan, Orakzai, Peshawar, Shangla, South Waziristan, Swat, Tank and Tor Ghar.

Gilgit-Baltistan: Astore and Diamir. 

 

VI. WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR NEXT 48-HOURS

  • Widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy to very heavy falls is expected over

Punjab: Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Chiniot, DG Khan, Faisalabad, Jhang, Kasur, Khanewal, Lahore, Layyah, Lodhran, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Nankana Sahib, Okara, Pakpattan, Rahim Yar Khan, Rajanpur, Sahiwal, Sheikhupura, Toba Tek Singh and Vehari. 

Sindh: Badin, Dadu, Ghotki, Hyderabad, Jacobabad, Jamshoro, Karachi, Kashmore, Khairpur, Larkana, Matiari, Mirpur Khas, Naushahro Feroze, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazir Abad, Sujawal, Sukkur, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta and Umer Kot. 

Balochistan: Dera Bugti, Harnai, Khuzdar, Kohlu, Nasirabad and Sibi.

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm isolated heavy falls is expected over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad, Kashmir

WEEKLY SIGNIFICANT OUTLOOK 

(01st August, 2026 to 7th August, 2026)

I. RAINFALL OUTLOOK

The current wet spell is expected to continue in the upper catchments of all the major rivers, Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Kashmir, Punjab, Sindh and east Balochistan uptill 04th August, 2026.

 

WARNING: 

  • Under the influence of an approaching depression, presently located over south Madhya Pradesh (India), a strong wet spell is expected to affect southern Punjab, southeastern Sindh and eastern Balochistan from 1st to 4th August. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also likely during this period.

  • Consequently, urban flooding, waterlogging, and prolonged water ponding are likely in Badin, Hyderabad, Jamshoro, Khairpur, Matiari, Mirpur Khas, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazirabad, Sujawal, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta, and Umerkot districts during the forecast period.

II. FLOOD OUTLOOK

  • The flows in the eastern rivers and associated tributaries are also expected to rise from 01st August to 04th August, 2026.

    WARNING: 

  • Medium to High level flows are expected in nullahs of Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Bassanter, Deg and Sakki). 

  • Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of DG Khan, the streams of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan.

  • Urban Flooding is also expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisalabad.

All figures in thousands of cusecs. Full bar = maximum (design) capacity.     • Medium to High level flows are expected in nullahs of Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Bassanter, Deg and Sakki). 

    • Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of DG Khan, the streams of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan.

    • Urban Flooding is also expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisalabad. 

       

II: METEOROLOGICAL FEATURES

  • Yesterday's trough of westerly wave over northeast Afghanistan today lies over northern part of the country.

  • Yesterday’s Deep Depression over northeast Orissa today lies over north east Chattisgarh (India) with central pressure (992 hPa). It is likely to move westwards over northeast Madhya Pradesh (India).

  • A vertically elongated seasonal low-pressure area with central pressure lies over Northeast Balochistan.

  • Moderate moist currents from Arabian sea and weak moist current from Bay of Bengal (along the foot hills of Himalayan mountains) are penetrating into upper parts of the country up to 5,000 feet.

III: WEATHER FORECAST FOR 24-HOURS

  • Widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy falls is expected over Islamabad, Kashmir

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Buner, Charsadda, DI Khan, Haripur, Karak, Kohat, Lakki Marwat, Mansehra, Mardan, Nowshera, Peshawar, Swabi and Tank. 

    Punjab: Rawalpindi, Attock, Bahawalnagar, Bhakkar, Chakwal, Chiniot, DG Khan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, Jhang, Jhelum, Kasur, Khanewal, Khushab, Lahore, Layyah, Mandi Bahauddin, Mianwali, Nankana Sahib, Narowal, Okara, Pakpattan, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Toba Tek Singh and Vehari. 

    Balochistan: Musakhel.

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the catchments of all major rivers, 

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Bajaur, Bannu, Batagram, Chitral, Dir, Hangu, Khyber, Kohistan, Kurram, Lower Dir, Mohmand, Orakzai, Shangla, Waziristan and Swat. 

    Balochistan: Barkhan, Duki, Harnai, Killa Saifullah, Kohlu, Loralai, Sherani, Zhob and Ziarat; 

    Gilgit-Baltistan: Astore, Darel, Diamir, Ghizer, Gilgit, Gupis-Yasin and Tangir. 

IV: WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR NEXT 48-HOURS

  • Widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy to very heavy falls is expected over the upper catchments of rivers Sutlej, Ravi and Chenab, Islamabad, Kashmir, 

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Bajaur, Bannu, Buner, Charsadda, DI Khan, Hangu, Haripur, Karak, Khyber, Kohat, Kurram, Lakki Marwat, Dir, Malakand, Mardan, Mohmand, Nowshera, Orakzai, Peshawar, Swabi, Waziristan and Tank. 

    Punjab: Rawalpindi, Attock, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Bhakkar, Chakwal, Chiniot, DG Khan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, Jhang, Jhelum, Kasur, Khanewal, Khushab, Lahore, Layyah, Lodhran, Mandi Bahauddin, Mianwali, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Nankana Sahib, Narowal, Okara, Pakpattan, Rajanpur, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Toba Tek Singh and Vehari. 

    Balochistan: Musakhel and Sherani. 

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the upper catchments of rivers Indus, Jhelum

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Batagram, Chitral, Kohistan, Mansehra, Shangla, Swat, Tor Ghar. 

    Punjab: Rahim Yar Khan. 

    Sindh: Badin, Ghotki, Khairpur, Mirpur Khas, Sanghar, Sujawal, Sukkur, Tando Allahyar, Tharparkar and Umer Kot. 

    Balochistan: Khuzdar. 

    Gilgit-Baltistan: Darel, Diamir and Tangir. 

     

2. WEEKLY WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR RIVER’S CATCHMENTS

(30th- July, 2026 to 5th- August, 2026)

RAINFALL OUTLOOK:

  • The current wet spell is likely to intensify from 30th July in upper catchments of all the major rivers,  and Sindh is likely to persist uptill 04th August, 2026.

  • WARNING: On account of upcoming strong monsoon incursions from both Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal, fairly widespread to widespread rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy to very heavy falls is expected over Islamabad, Punjab, Kashmir, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit Baltistan and southeast Sindh. Consequently, river flows are likely to increase in significantly in all major rivers upto 04th August.

 

FLOOD SITUATION IN MAJOR RIVERS:

  • River Indus at Guddu has attained Medium flood level at upstream. Whereas, Sukkur will remain in Low flood level during next 24-hours, after that it will also attain medium flood level at upstream. 

  • The flows in the eastern rivers and associated tributaries ae also expected to rise from 30th July till 04th August, 2026.

  • WARNING: 

    • Medium to High level flows are expected in nullahs of Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Bassanter, Deg and Sakki). 

    • Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of DG Khan, the streams of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan.

    • Urban Flooding is also expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisalabad. 

Page break

3. WEATHER/RAINFALL FORECAST FOR NEXT 24-HRS

4. QUANTITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST OF GAUGING STATIONS (IN THOUSANDS OF CUSECS)

Spatial: Isolated=20 to 30% of area | Scattered=31 to 50% of area | Fairly Widespread=51 to 75% of area | Widespread=76 to 100% of area, R= Rising, F=Falling

Intensity (mm/24 hours): Light ≤ 10, Moderate =10.1 – 30, Heavy=30.1 – 70, Very Heavy=70.1 - 150, Extremely Heavy > 150

Note: Concerned Departments may contact FFD, Lahore for rectification up-dation (if any)

5. HOW CLOSE IS EACH RIVER TO ITS LIMIT?

Guddu is in medium flood at 383.7 — 116.3 below its high flood level (500.0). Each bar is one station’s own flood levels across its maximum capacity; the solid run is the flow so far, the pale run is the room still left.

All figures in thousands of cusecs. Full bar = maximum (design) capacity. Solid colour is the flow reached so far and the pale wash beside it is the room still left; the dark line between them is the current reading, printed beneath it. Thin white lines are that station’s flood levels with their thresholds beneath, so the same colour can begin at a different point on every bar. Each band is named inside itself — initialled (BL, L, M, H, VH, EH) where the band is too narrow for the words, and left blank where it is too narrow for those. Stations without a design capacity are not shown.
